newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Spain helps Bulgaria seize killers of policemen.
newsitem.headline: Spain helps Bulgaria seize killers of policemen.

text.p: Bulgaria's interior ministry said on Monday the suspected killers of three Bulgarian policemen, whose gangland murder cost the interior minister his job, had been captured with the help of Spanish police.

"After the initial shock of this outrageous murder we launched a strong investigation and with the cooperation of the Spanish police we managed to arrest the two killers," ministry official Yordan Maslarev told a news conference.
The three policemen were shot dead on May 3 in a Sofia suburb as they tried to arrest the two killers, who had been suspected of threatening to kill an interior ministry employee.
The shootings provoked strong public outrage that led to the resignation of interior minister Lyubomir Nachev.
Maslarev, who headed the investigation, said the first suspect had been arrested last month in Sofia after a nationwide hunt. The second was caught last Thursday in Madrid.

"Both of the murderers have long police records and have been involved in a series of crimes, mainly heavy armed robberies," Maslarev said. Spain was expected to extradite the murderer within 40 days.

Like other east European countries Bulgaria has seen a sharp escalation in violent crime in recent years as it moves from a planned to a free market economy. Cash-strapped police are often poorly equipped to battle ruthless, well-organised criminal gangs.
